question: Does FREQ-defined rare-allele information improve diploid ancestry-dose prediction beyond calibrated B0 and same-locus ancestry-label shams?

rare_universe.definition: minor allele with MAC>=2, MAF<0.01 and at least two carrier individuals in FREQ; FREQ alone defines rarity
rare_universe.operational_observability: retain for modeling only FREQ-defined sites with at least one minor copy in pooled REF_LAI; REF_LAI never defines rarity

arms.B0_CAL: B0 diploid posteriors plus four constant-zero columns
arms.BR: same B0 posteriors plus target rare load and three real REF_LAI ancestry-support channels
arms.BSHAM: same exact B0, rare loci, positions, target genotypes, missingness, load and LD as BR; only complete-individual REF_LAI ancestry labels are permuted

model.C_selection: apply the same mean-bidirectional DEV rule separately to B0_CAL, BR, and independently to each BSHAM replicate; the null repeats the complete tuning operation

evaluation.primary: equal-individual mean of genetic-length-weighted macro ancestry-proportion MAE
evaluation.boundary_policy: not estimated in DEV because diploid window posteriors do not identify phased haplotype boundaries; do not impute phase
evaluation.gate: BR improvement over B0_CAL must be positive and exceed the 95th percentile of BSHAM improvements in both directions

stop_rule: STOP before any VALID/TEST access if either direction fails, any provenance hash fails, an ancestry class is lost, convergence fails, or same-locus identity fails.
